p: Vulcan Road is tucked into the Meadowhall area in the Don Valley, and the name's a nice nod to the city's past: Vulcan was the Roman god of fire and metalworking, and Sheffield has a statue of him on top of the Town Hall. This whole valley was once wall-to-wall steelworks, and that history is never far away.

Getting here without a car is easy. Meadowhall Interchange brings together trains, Supertram and buses, so you can hop over from the city centre or from Rotherham and Barnsley without worrying about parking.

If you want to see what made Sheffield famous, Kelham Island Museum is the place to go. It tells the story of the city's steel and cutlery trades, and its giant River Don Engine is a huge steam engine that has to be seen to be believed. It's a great pick for kids who like big machines.

In the city centre, the Winter Garden is a glasshouse full of plants from around the world, and it sits right next to the Peace Gardens, where children love running through the fountains on a warm day. Weston Park Museum, near the university, is free and has everything from natural history to a gallery about Sheffield life, while the Botanical Gardens are a peaceful spot for a picnic.
If your crew are into music or sport, the Utilita Arena and the Ponds Forge area host big events through the year, so check what's on if you fancy turning a jump session into an evening out.

A handy way to plan the day is to bounce first, then hop on the tram into town for lunch and a museum. Everyone gets their energy out early, and the afternoon becomes a bit calmer and a lot more civilised.
